Subject: Consolidated quote dissection and rollback options

Hi Helen / Amit,

Thanks again for the time earlier — appreciated the candor on runtime fit and the migration window. I attached the consolidated SOW and a short runbook/estimate that breaks down where the quoted delta shows up (token economics, dedicated buffer, egress sensitivity).

Two specific asks from our side to keep momentum:
- Can you confirm the primary procurement constraints (pricing floor, required term, approval timeline)?
- Would a short, timeboxed rollback/escape credit help your internal risk team accept a 12-month commitment? We can propose a hybrid solution: match the quoted unit price for core inference tokens, plus a one-time migration credit to offset integration work.

Attachments: ClearBay_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW), runbook_costs.xlsx (breakout)

If you’re OK, I’ll pull together a formal concession structure and loop in legal for a redline.

Next steps: I’m free tomorrow early afternoon PT for a 20-minute sync.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim

From: Amit Shah <amit@clearbay.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Helen Cho <procurement@clearbay.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated quote dissection and rollback options

Rachel —

Thanks for the SOW and runbook. A few points from procurement/security that will affect any concession:
1) We cannot increase our committed spend beyond the internal budget; any concession has to be neutral to year-one cash outflow.
2) Migration credits are acceptable if they are tied to measurable milestones (pilot acceptance tests).
3) Our security team will require a compatibility checklist for KV cache persistence and a brief on how Redwood handles cold starts and pre-warming for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Also attaching a short procurement checklist (proc_requirements.pdf) — it lists our approval gates and a vendor continuity clause we typically insist on.

If you can present a structure that keeps year-one cash flat while offering operational risk mitigation (migration credit + rollback option), we can present it to finance next week.

Best,
Amit Shah
VP, Platform Engineering
ClearBay Health
amit@clearbay.com

Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Jul 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consolidated quote dissection and rollback options — proposed structure

Amit / Helen —

Appreciate the clarity. Based on procurement constraints, here is a straight-forward structure that keeps your year-one cash neutral while addressing operational risk:

1) Unit price match: Redwood will match the unit inference price for the base 12-month committed volume (matches the line-item in the competing quote).
2) Migration credit: one-time credit equal to 3 months of expected spend (applied as invoice credit over the first 90 days), contingent on pilot acceptance.
3) Rollback protection: if the pilot fails the acceptance tests we’ll provide a 60-day termination assistance credit and pay for exporter tooling to move KV/embeddings (capped).
4) Dedicated pilot: provide a 30-day dedicated pool (2 GPUs equivalent) for acceptance tests at no charge — we’ll instrument latency and token breakdowns for your team.

Technical note for your security team: our KV cache is compatible with open formats (RocksDB snapshot plus an export tool); pre-warm is handled via a warmup stream that primes common prefixes and reduces cold-start tail latency. Happy to have our infra folks join the technical call.

If that structure looks OK I’ll ask Connor to produce a numeric concession sheet and Marissa to prepare contract language for the rollback clause.

Thanks,
Rachel

Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Consolidated quote dissection and rollback options — concession math

Rachel / Marissa —

I ran the numbers off Rachel's proposed structure. Quick summary (high level):
- Baseline committed ARR per ClearBay’s target: $1,200,000
- If we match unit price, expected revenue delta is ~ -$120k vs quoted list in year one (we absorb margin via efficiency).
- Migration credit (3 months): ~ $90k (applied as invoice credit)
- Dedicated 30-day pilot (2x A100-equivalent) incremental cost to Redwood: ~$18k (we can absorb as marketing/pilot credit)

Net P&L impact year-one (if we accept): approximately -$132k before renewals.

Recommended concession envelope: cap total credits/assistance to $125k; require pilot acceptance criteria in writing; require a 12-month minimum (to protect renewal math). Also include a rollback cap for exporter costs ($25k).

I attached a short workbook (runbook_costs.xlsx) with the line-item math and suggested invoice schedule.

If Marissa can draft a rollback clause with the caps and pilot acceptance milestones I think this is presentable to ClearBay procurement while keeping within our commercial thresholds.

—Connor
Principal Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 17 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Consolidated quote dissection and rollback options — draft language

Connor / Rachel —

Draft language draft attached (I can paste into Docusign redline once we agree):
- Term: 12 months minimum for the matched unit pricing.
- Migration credit: one-time invoice credit equal to three months expected spend; applied over first two invoices; not refundable.
- Pilot acceptance: defined by performance SLA (p95 latency < 120ms on production-like workload) and correctness tests (sample inference accuracy on provided prompt set).
- Rollback assistance: Redwood to provide export tooling and up to $25,000 in migration assistance costs if pilot fails; Redwood will not be liable for downstream data transformation costs beyond that cap.
- Audit & security: Redwood to provide a short technical appendix describing KV export format, pre-warm mechanism, and SOC2 evidence references.

I’ll mark optional clauses for negotiation (pilot duration, rollback cap). If we’re aligned I’ll upload the redline to DocuSign and Rachel can circulate the link to ClearBay.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
